System Map

Read together, the four parts of the theme are not separate pressures. Four loops connect them: a congestion brake in which inland cargo meets strained rail and gates, an automation squeeze in which fewer dockworker shifts meet peak demand, a grid-dependent yard in which electric terminals turn power cuts into stops, and a seeing-the-risk loop in which losses fund the evidence that prevents them. Arrows that cross a colour are connections no single part carries.

Swipe sideways to see the whole map.

LoopNameWhat it doesThis cycle
B1Congestion brake
Critical dependencies		More cargo moving inland raises congestion at the gates and on rail, and congestion pushes cargo to rival ports.Priming: trains down 14.2%
R1Automation squeeze
Technology and adaptation		Automation cuts dockworker shifts, thinner crews struggle at peaks, and peak delays strengthen the case for more automation.Priming: shifts falling to 112,834
R2Grid-dependent yard
Critical dependencies		Automation and shore power raise the port’s dependence on the grid, power cuts become stops, stops become backlogs, and backlogs push more automation.Priming: 132 MW substation planned
B2Seeing the risk
Technology and adaptation		Stops and losses raise demand for evidence of exposure, evidence funds a live picture of risk, and a live picture cuts unplanned stops.Priming: 31 satellites, static model

Hover over a status for its meaning: Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks how much load B1 Congestion brake must carry, that is whether Genoa stays a transhipment hub or becomes an inland gateway; its vertical axis asks whether B2 Seeing the risk is built for the whole port or terminal by terminal.

What it means: Every outside switch on the map lands on a link the port does not own, so the levers that matter most are shared: a dependency register with the infrastructure operators, common weather rules among the terminals, and a live picture of risk that all of them can see.
